title: Prefixcache stress probe: tail-latency vs hit-rate vs resident-memory
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable, CI-friendly stress probe that maps prefix cache hit-rate to end-to-end tail latency and resident memory under realistic ML inference traffic. This ticket implements the harness, statistical regression checks, and a Grafana dashboard for nightly comparisons.

Motivation:
- Current benchmarks show average throughput but under-emphasize tail behavior and working-set memory pressure as hit-rate changes.
- We need an actionable regression detector to block PRs or trigger alerts when a change meaningfully worsens p95/p99 or increases memory usage beyond cost thresholds.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Reproducible harness that can run on nightly CI and per-PR with a small smoke profile.
- Metrics emitted: tokens_per_sec, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, kv_hit_rate, resident_set_bytes, gpu_mem_bytes, cpu_user_seconds, eviction_rate, kv_lookup_latency_ms.
- Baseline nightly job stores baseline distributions; regression rule flags if p95 increases >10% and the change is statistically significant (Mann-Whitney U with p<0.01 or bootstrap CI non-overlap).
- Dashboard tile showing hit-rate vs p95 vs resident memory, with heatmap and iso-lines for tokens/sec.
- PR check integration: a lightweight run with the same workload shape that fails CI on confirmed regressions.

Testbed & methodology:
- Hardware: testbed runs on T4-equivalent and A4000-equivalent VMs (to cover mid and low tiers).
- Workloads: three synthetic mixes - ShortPrefix (seq=64, batch=8, high reuse), LongPrefix (seq=1024, batch=1, low reuse), MixedBurst (mixed seqs, Poisson arrivals).
- Key parameters: concurrency (8/32/128), batch sizes (1/8/32), prefix cardinality (1k/10k/100k unique prefixes), working-set sizes (50MB/200MB/1GB), eviction policies (LRU/clock-prob).
- Warm/cold scenarios: cold start (empty cache), warm steady-state (preload target working-set), and churn (continuous inserts to exercise evictions).
- Measurement windows: 5m ramp, 15m sample, 5m cool-down. Repeat 3 runs per configuration and aggregate distributions.

Implementation notes:
- Reuse existing toy harness code but replace sampling with a new 'prefill-autogen' workload that deterministically seeds prefixes to reach target hit-rates instead of ad-hoc random seeding. This reduces noise for regression detection.
- Memory accounting: use OS resident set (smem) + custom allocator hooks for KV slab usage. Report both aggregate and per-process breakdown to detect leaks vs expected working-set growth.
- Latency collection: per-request end-to-end timestamps plus internal KV lookup timings to isolate where tail is introduced. Store traces for top 0.1% requests.
- Regression detection pipeline: nightly job pushes sample distributions to S3 as NDJSON; Lambda job runs statistical tests and writes a regression note to the benchmark index; Slack/GitHub integration posts a summary.

Operational knobs to expose later to Console/Optimize team:
- Target hit-rate and working-set size sliders for quick experiments.
- Cost estimation: map resident memory -> expected GPU density and per-token cost.

Artifacts and deliverables:
- harness: perf/prefix_stress_probe.py (runs locally and in CI)
- config: perf/configs/prefix_profiles.yml with canonical mixes
- dashboard: grafana/dashboards/prefixcache_hit_latency.json
- regression job: ci/benchmarks/prefix_regression_job.yaml
- PR gating: .github/workflows/bench-smoke.yml

Notes on statistical thresholds (internal decision):
- We debated absolute vs relative thresholds. Chosen default: relative (pct) thresholds to scale across models. Default alert: p95_pct_change > 10% AND Mann-Whitney p < 0.01. For small-sample PR runs use bootstrap CI and require non-overlap at 95% CI.

Risks & constraints:
- Synthetic workloads may miss real-world burst patterns; we'll pair this with sampled production replay after this spike is stable.
- Memory accounting across container boundaries is noisy on some hypervisors; add host-side measurement agent where possible.

Next steps:
1) Deliver harness proto and minimal dashboard (this ticket).
2) Add PR-gating lightweight profile and integrate with perf-as-check.
3) Iterate on threshold tuning with 2 weeks of nightly baselines.

Customer impact: medium (regressions here affect latency SLAs for customers using prefix caching).
